The grepped files (applier.py, fetcher.py, run_differs.py, _attestation.py, apply_inbound_records.py) are executable SOURCE UNDER TEST, not instruction artifacts consumed by a non-human parser — so the Rule-5 structural-artifact exception does not apply.

Litmus (Rule 4): a behavior-preserving edit — e.g. adding `AcliClient(` inside a docstring example, or an unrelated second `"jira"` literal — would break these assertions with no observable-behavior change.
advisory.finding: test_backend_neutrality.py asserts on the SOURCE TEXT of the modules under test (`"AcliClient(" not in text` for applier.py/fetcher.py/run_differs.py/_attestation.py, and `text.count('"jira"') == 1` for apply_inbound_records.py). These read the source under test as the assertion rather than exercising behavior — a change-detector that breaks on any behavior-preserving edit (e.g. an `AcliClient(` reference added to a docstring/comment, or a second legitimate `"jira"` string literal) without any observable-behavior regression. It is the source-grepping antipattern (grepping SOURCE CODE UNDER TEST, not a non-executable instruction artifact).
